assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: portrait key art / game cover, 1024x1536 composition.
Create a finished cover concept for a monochrome Playdate cooking game. Working title exactly "BUN RUSH", large in two tightly stacked lines at the top, original bold condensed ink lettering with a slight forward lean; clearly legible as a small thumbnail. No other text.
Reference image 1 (patty) and 2 (American cheese) are STYLE AND FOOD MATERIAL references; image 3 is the actual game's hand-cranked grinder silhouette. Use their coarse black-and-white pixel-edged stipple, halftone and cutout aesthetic, realistic food proportions and draping cheese. Do not copy their blank compositions.
One appetizing oversized burger is the main subject, three-quarter low view, slightly precarious with sesame top bun, one visibly draped cheese slice, two grilled patties, lettuce and tomato, all clearly layered. A few separated ingredients above it suggest frantic assembly without exploding the whole burger. At its base on a work counter: the recognizable small manual meat grinder on the lower left and a modest frying grate with one small flame on the lower right. A tiny pair of blank curling order slips connects the bustle, with minimal motion strokes. No people, no mascots, no faces on food. No vehicles.
Composition: title dominates upper quarter, burger dominates middle, small workstation elements anchor bottom, generous clean off-white/white negative space separating silhouettes. Monochrome BLACK AND WHITE ONLY, gray values suggested exclusively by deliberately coarse dots and broken ink. Hand-made early Macintosh / Playdate 1-bit editorial food illustration, not smooth vector cartoon, not cute, not glossy 3D, no gradients, no photorealistic lighting. Strong black silhouette edges with interior dotted texture; keep letter interiors mostly solid for readability. No device mockup, no outer picture frame, no watermark, no publisher logo. This is a standalone full-bleed cover artwork.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-screen Playdate game MAIN MENU concept, one flat 5:3 landscape image, ideally 1600x960 representing a 400x240 game screen at 4x. NOT a poster, NOT a device mockup.
Input reference 1 is the matching BUN RUSH cover: preserve its original chunky italic black title letterforms, realistic food proportions, draped cheese, coarse monochrome stipple and ink outlines. Recompose for an extremely legible small monochrome game display. No other game title.
Layout in logical 400x240 coordinates:
White background. Left column x24..205. At top x24 y20 a large two-line wordmark "BUN" above "RUSH", total width180 and height88. Keep both complete words wholly inside the frame. A few tiny horizontal speed marks are allowed beside the wordmark.
Below the logo at y140, a solid triangular selector followed by the exact menu label "START SHIFT", a sturdy legible 12px-equivalent black block font, all on white. At y169 another option "HOW TO PLAY" in the same font, no selector. No black-filled selection rectangle.
Bottom left at y218 a small but legible instruction "A: SELECT".
Right column x225..387: one large partly assembled double-patty burger with its bun hovering only slightly, crisp lettuce, one draped cheese slice and readable meat textures. Keep the burger separate from the text, in the same appetizing inky style as the cover. Anchor it with a little countertop near y208. One small realistic crank grinder silhouette sits near the far lower right. Keep imagery away from menu text. Omit the cover's flying slips and crowded grill so the screen remains calm and readable.
Everything strictly black ink and white paper; shading via coarse black dot patterns only. Draw the illustration with graphic simplification appropriate to a 400x240 1-bit screen: no tiny decorative stippling that overwhelms silhouettes. No gray gradients, no color, no soft shadows, no 3D rendering, no cartoon faces, no people. Thin clean whitespace gutters. Do not include game HUD, scores, extra buttons, labels, frame, watermark, handheld console or presentation caption. The deliverable is the actual rectangular main-menu screen concept.
